description:
On Windows, tests that read repository text files with the default code page raise UnicodeDecodeError ('charmap' codec), because pathlib read_text() without an encoding uses the locale encoding.

Current failures: 12 tests in 6 files, from the Windows 3.12 fast-test step of run 37967682464:
- tests/unit/workflows/test_t2_partition_workflow.py:15 (6 tests; workflow YAML read)
- tests/unit/platforms/test_physical_identifier_resolution.py:172
- tests/unit/platforms/test_physical_identifier_resolution_databricks_bigquery.py:222
- tests/unit/platforms/test_post_load_seam.py:245
- tests/unit/scripts/test_agent_instruction_audit.py (Makefile case of test_handback_guard_covers_the_scripts_and_docs_that_print_guidance, around line 299; the audit reads the Makefile without an encoding)
- tests/unit/scripts/test_pr_arm.py:245 (Makefile read; moved here from nightly-windows-path-quoting-20261008)

Fix: pass encoding="utf-8" to each read_text() and open() call that reads repository text, and decode subprocess output explicitly.

Prevention: ruff PLW1514 is enabled (pyproject.toml:434) but cannot type pathlib read_text(), so it does not catch these calls. scripts/check_windows_antipatterns.py already flags read_text() without an encoding, but _DEFAULT_ROOTS = ["benchbox"] (line 33) limits it to the package. Extend it to tests/ and scripts/ with a ratchet: tests/ and scripts/ currently hold 358 such calls in 133 files, so a hard fail would need a baseline that may only shrink.

Alternative: set PYTHONUTF8=1 in the Windows job. That is a one-line change and fixes every such read at once. The tradeoff is that it hides the defect: the tests would pass while real users on a non-UTF-8 code page still hit it, and it makes the Windows leg differ from a normal user environment.
